events.text: I am painting an original red enamel camping mug with rising steam, sparked by the NPS Cooking in Camp guide. Goal: broad joined warm planes, a continuous curved rim, and one short focal reflection. I will leave quieter wood and soft steam around the cup.
The first washes left bright channels. Overlapping passes will join the cool backdrop and warm tabletop before the red cup arrives.
The gaps are closed; soft horizontal wash seams remain. I will set the contact shadow and a broad dark red cup mass, keeping the handle open to the backdrop.
The cup body is hollow at the center and the shadow is a rigid bar. Broad crosswise red planes will fill the body first; the open handle stays untouched for now.
Crosswise red closed most of the hole, but a pale slit remains. I will bridge that slit with a loaded plane and establish the dark oval mouth.
The body is now filled. The mouth is continuous but faceted and the handle thin. I will thicken the handle with many-point curves and give the red wall a warmer left turn.
The many-point handle gives a warmer inner curve, though the original polygon remains outside it. The rim needs an enamel edge and the lower body needs a quieter reflected plane.
The pale rim is continuous, but the new right shadow is a stripe. A broader middle red will soften that join. I will also replace the rigid shadow bar with a wider muted tabletop shadow.
The shadow widened but retained its dark bar and ridges; the narrow red cover only partly softened the stripe. I will keep these as evidence and test soft watercolor steam against the blue ground.
The steam is faint and soft at whole view, unlike the hard oil rim. I will keep that contrast. Long tabletop grain and a low folded cloth will give the cup a more grounded setting.
The cloth block-in is hollow like the early cup. Broad diagonal overlaps will close it, then a darker fold can describe its turn without outlining every edge.
The cloth is filled and its fold reads as a strong blue diagonal. I will lay a small spoon across it, using a dark base and muted metal so it stays below the mug in emphasis.
The spoon reads at whole view and remains subdued. The blank lower left can carry a small fallen pine sprig, with a curved stem and unequal needles rather than another outlined object.
The first pine marks look like blunt sticks. Finer unequal fans will break those ends and connect them to the curved stem.
Fine fans make the sprig less rigid, but it needs needles below the stem and a finer upper cluster. I will vary their lengths and keep them dark enough to stay secondary.
Lower review: the sprig now has unequal fans, and the spoon is readable against filled cloth. The cloth fold is still a strong blue bar; I will narrow its middle and join the spoon bowl.
Returning to the cup: the red wall has a dark vertical stripe and a flat central light. Broader warm planes should join those passages before any small enamel chips or focal light.
Broader warm planes joined the center, while the dark stripe persists. I will turn it into a narrower edge by covering from the lit side, and strengthen the handle attachments.
The stripe is narrower and the handle joins more solidly. I will break the uniform rim light into quieter and brighter sections, with small dark enamel chips rather than an unbroken white outline.
I will test one short loaded warm reflection on the left shoulder. It should stay compact at whole view and remain separate from the quieter rim light.
The single shoulder reflection is compact and visible. I will keep it. Three quieter touches will turn the coffee surface and soften the lower red plane without adding another bright accent.
The focal light holds; the coffee remains a dark oval. The steam disappears above its first turn, so I will strengthen only the lower curves and let their upper ends dissolve.
The steam remains subtle. Crossed watery background gestures may interrupt the horizontal seam without sharpening the quiet backdrop; I will keep them away from the focal cup.
Crossed washes broke the upper stripe into broad diagonal shapes, while the middle seam remains. I will now soften the cast-shadow ends with loaded tabletop color, testing coverage locally.
The shadow ends are partly muted but enlarged ridged patches remain. I will leave the central contact dark and connect the table grain around the sprig with broken, lower-contrast gestures.
Final refinement begins with the handle: its outer polygon is still too mechanical. A many-point red edge and muted interior cover will soften two corners without closing the opening.
The handle is warmer and rounder inside; the outer polygon persists and the interior cover left a short blue line. I will avoid more widening and taper the blunt pine ends instead.
The needle extensions are slight at whole view. Final corrections will quiet the blue handle-cover line and unify the lower cup turn, preserving the short shoulder light.

The handle covers added ridged islands; more paint there is unlikely to help. Last refinement: join the warm shoulder below the focal light and quiet the lower reflection while keeping the continuous rim.

Finished at 112 marks: Red mug, morning hush. Broad joined red planes, continuous enamel rim and one compact shoulder light meet the practice goal. Soft steam stays quiet. Angular handle, cast-shadow bar, regular ridges and failed handle-cover islands remain; further covering is widening shapes rather than clarifying them. Human ratings remain unset.

creation.method: AI agent painting through local Atelier browser in animated 1–4-stroke batches chosen after paired settled screenshot inspections.
creation.inspectionEvidence: 29 settled paired whole-and-close screenshot boundaries, including single-mark reflection check at 77; lower preset pan at 60 centered on cup base and did not show side objects closely. At 8, generic locator failed and initial close crop used transformed canvas bounds; corrected to measured canvas-wrap bounds and repeated pair before more painting. At 12, early rest check failed; waited for completion before paired inspection. All unique JPEG pairs retained locally, final pair committed. Camera waited 900ms and verified 2.0×. Actual browser PNG 900x620 visually inspected.
creation.notes: 30 easel notes posted live; creation metadata and practice entry retrospective.

inspiration.description: NPS Cooking in Camp guide sparked an original imagined red enamel mug, steam, pine sprig and spoon on a folded cloth. No finished composition copied.

creation.stoppingDecision: Stopped after deliberate 100–112 refinement and paired final review. Joined warm planes, continuous rim and short focal reflection hold; watercolor steam stays soft. Handle covers added ridged islands and shadow covers enlarged patches. More covering is unlikely to help. Angular handle, shadow bar, wash seams and regular simulated ridges remain.
